input.rationale: The retained finding's one recorded counterevidence is that the probe constructed its large replay windows by disabling automatic snapshotting, which leaves open whether the captured default snapshot cadence (SnapshotThreshold 8192, SnapshotInterval 120s) would have kept the window below the 128-batch bound. This submission revises the fixed experiment on exactly that point: the snapshot settings stay untouched at their configured values and are reported as operands, the newest snapshot is placed with a real user snapshot so the accumulation after it is deterministic, and one case has no snapshot at all, which is the state of a node that has not yet reached its first periodic check. Source anchors for the interval-driven check (snapshot.go) are added for the account that will interpret the receipt. No interpretation is appended here because the answer to the registered gap must come from the retained execution of this revision, not from a prediction.

scope.description: Three restart-only cases over the real hashicorp/raft single-voter node with the captured snapshot settings left in place (in-memory transport, real commit-tracking log store): commit with the actual leader, optionally place the newest snapshot with a real user snapshot at a chosen index, commit more entries, stop the node, then call NewRaft again over the unchanged stores with a fresh transport on the same address and record whether it returns.
assumptions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the documented opt-in configuration for the feature under test.

SnapshotThreshold, SnapshotInterval and MaxAppendEntries are not modified by the harness; their configured values are reported in the admission event so the reader can check that the defaults were in force.

The test runs for seconds, well inside the configured 120s snapshot interval, so the periodic check does not fire during the case; that is the situation in which the window is whatever accumulated since the newest snapshot, and the case without a snapshot is the situation of a node before its first periodic check.

A returning restart is expected in the millisecond range; the 5s wait is a ceiling for recording non-return, and non-return cases additionally carry the stack of the goroutine left in the startup replay path.
Restarted instances use a null logger so no logging occurs after the test completes; logging is not part of the observed mechanism.
excluded: Real-time accumulation over a full 120s interval is not observed; the accumulation is produced deterministically by the target's own apply path instead, and the rate at which the same accumulation would occur in time is left as arithmetic on the configured interval.
Multi-voter clusters, network faults, on-disk log stores and FSM slowness are excluded.
No production code is modified and no full-package suite is run; only the TestAssurance-prefixed test in this harness is selected.

parameters.cases: defaults_no_snapshot_window_10000(applied=10000, no snapshot), defaults_snapshot_then_10000_more(applied=14000, user snapshot after 4000), defaults_snapshot_then_2000_more(applied=6000, user snapshot after 4000)
parameters.events: startup_replay_prefix (applied, snapshot_after, max_append_entries, snapshot_threshold, snapshot_interval_ms, fsm_mutate_ch_capacity read from the running instance, persisted_commit_index, last_log_index, snapshot_present, snapshot_index, last_applied_before_restart, replay_window, fsm_bound_entries_in_window, estimated_replay_batches) and startup_replay_restart (the same operands plus replay_batches_within_capacity, restart_returned, restart_elapsed_ms, restart_error, restart_stack_frames)
parameters.predicted_window: persisted_commit_index minus the newest snapshot index, counted in FSM-bound entries, with the captured SnapshotThreshold of 8192 and a 120s interval in force

experiment.prefix: Each case builds one real single-voter cluster with opts{Peers:1, Bootstrap:true, CommitTrackingLogs:true} and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, leaving SnapshotThreshold=8192, SnapshotInterval=120s and MaxAppendEntries=64 as configured. Commands are applied through the leader's normal path, with a real user snapshot (leader.Snapshot()) inserted after the chosen number of applies when a case asks for one, so the newest snapshot in the store and the entries above it are produced by the target itself. Before shutdown the harness reads the store's persisted commit index, the last log index, the newest snapshot from the store list, cap(fsmMutateCh), the configured MaxAppendEntries, SnapshotThreshold and SnapshotInterval, and censuses the entry types in the replay window with GetLog using the same rule as Raft.prepareLog, then emits the startup_replay_prefix event. It then shuts the node down, creates a fresh NewInmemTransport on the same address and calls NewRaft over the unchanged logs/stable/snapshots instances as the target's own restart tests do, in a goroutine that reports completion through a channel; it waits up to 5s, and if nothing arrived it samples all goroutine stacks and keeps the one on the startup replay path. It finally emits the startup_replay_restart event carrying the same operands plus replay_batches_within_capacity and the outcome.

comparisons.description: With the configured snapshot settings in force, a restart whose committed-but-unapplied window needs at most fsm_mutate_ch_capacity batches returns.

With the configured snapshot settings in force but a window above the configured SnapshotThreshold accumulated since the newest snapshot, NewRaft does not return within the bounded wait and a goroutine is left in the startup replay path.

experiment.revision_reason: Changed basis to address the recorded counterevidence: the predecessor disabled automatic snapshotting (SnapshotThreshold=MaxUint64, SnapshotInterval=1h) and varied MaxAppendEntries and applied counts; this revision leaves SnapshotThreshold, SnapshotInterval and MaxAppendEntries at their configured values, reports them as observed operands, places the newest snapshot with a real user snapshot at a chosen point, and includes a case with no snapshot at all. The comparisons are the same predicates over the same admission prefix shape, so the receipt answers whether the configured snapshot cadence keeps the window below the bound.

scope.description: Five restart-only cases over the real hashicorp/raft single-voter node (in-memory transport, real commit-tracking log store): produce a committed log with the actual leader, stop the node, then call NewRaft again over the unchanged stores with a fresh transport on the same address, and record whether NewRaft returns. Cases vary only the size of the committed-but-unapplied startup replay window (applies before the restart, plus an optional manual snapshot before shutdown) and MaxAppendEntries.
assumptions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, which is the documented opt-in configuration for this feature.

Automatic snapshotting is disabled (SnapshotThreshold=math.MaxUint64, SnapshotInterval=1h) so the replay window is set explicitly instead of by timer; this models a node whose newest snapshot lags its commit index, which the default 120s SnapshotInterval plus 8192 SnapshotThreshold also produce at higher write rates.
Restarted instances are constructed with a null logger so that no logging occurs after the test completes; logging is not part of the observed mechanism.
The bounded 5s wait is not the evidence: a returning restart is expected to be ~ms, and the blocked case is additionally recorded as a goroutine stack in the startup replay path.
excluded: Multi-voter clusters, network faults, and on-disk (bolt) log stores are excluded; the mechanism observed is in the startup replay path, not in replication.
The FSM's own semantics are excluded: MockFSM only records applied logs, and no FSM behavior is asserted.

experiments.revision_reason: The predecessor harness emitted CA_EVENT payloads without an event name, so the retained run was recorded entirely as invalid_observation (parse loss, indices 0-4) and no comparison could be evaluated. This revision names the events, splits them into a pre-restart admission event and a restart result event so the restart outcome is admitted by an independently observed prefix, declares the two comparisons the hypothesis predicts, and adds two boundary cases that straddle 128 batches with otherwise identical setup.

materials.text:
applyCh:               applyCh,
		fsm:                   fsm,
		fsmMutateCh:           make(chan interface{}, 128),
		fsmSnapshotCh:         make(chan *reqSnapshotFuture),
		leaderCh:              make(chan bool, 1),

func DefaultConfig() *Config {
	return &Config{
		ProtocolVersion:    ProtocolVersionMax,
		HeartbeatTimeout:   1000 * time.Millisecond,
		ElectionTimeout:    1000 * time.Millisecond,
		CommitTimeout:      50 * time.Millisecond,
		MaxAppendEntries:   64,
		ShutdownOnRemove:   true,
		TrailingLogs:       10240,
		SnapshotInterval:   120 * time.Second,
		SnapshotThreshold:  8192,
		LeaderLeaseTimeout: 500 * time.Millisecond,
		LogLevel:           "DEBUG",
	}
}

result.summary: Targeted the one recorded counterevidence of the landed finding: the previous probe forced large replay windows by disabling automatic snapshotting, which left open whether the captured default cadence (SnapshotThreshold 8192, SnapshotInterval 120s) keeps the window below the 128-batch capacity. Submitted a successor experiment (using the unchanged clean harness mechanism) in which SnapshotThreshold, SnapshotInterval and MaxAppendEntries are left at their configured values and reported as observed operands, the newest snapshot is placed by a real user snapshot at a chosen index so the post-snapshot accumulation is deterministic, and one case has no snapshot at all — the state of a node that has not yet reached its first periodic check. Also added source anchors for the interval-driven snapshot check (runSnapshots' timer, shouldSnapshot's delta/threshold test, takeSnapshot) so the gap can be answered from the receipt plus that source account. Verified locally with native feedback before submitting: with the defaults untouched, 10000 commits with no snapshot give a replay window of 10001 entries / 157 batches and NewRaft does not return, a real snapshot at 4002 followed by 9998 more commits gives a window of 9998 / 157 batches and also does not return, while the same snapshot followed by only 1998 commits gives 1998 / 32 batches and returns in 1ms — so the configured snapshot settings do not cap the window, and the same non-return is reachable under the defaults rather than only with snapshots switched off. No interpretation is appended this turn: the gap answer must come from the retained execution of this revision, and the paused TimeoutNow authority lead stays paused until its resume conditions hold.

Cases vary the size of the committed-but-unapplied startup replay window (applies before the restart, plus an optional manual snapshot before shutdown) and MaxAppendEntries, which together decide how many FSM batches the replay must place in the 128-slot fsmMutateCh.
assumptions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, the documented opt-in configuration for this feature.

Automatic snapshotting is disabled (SnapshotThreshold=math.MaxUint64, SnapshotInterval=1h) so the replay window is set explicitly instead of by timer; this models a node whose newest snapshot lags its commit index, which the default 120s SnapshotInterval plus 8192 SnapshotThreshold also produce when more than 8192 entries are committed between snapshot checks.
Restarted instances are constructed with a null logger so no logging occurs after the test completes; logging is not part of the observed mechanism.

A returning restart is expected in the millisecond range, and the 5s wait is a ceiling for recording non-return, not the evidence for it: the non-return cases are additionally recorded with the stack of the goroutine left in the startup replay path.

The census of FSM-bound entries applies the Raft.prepareLog rule to the stored entries (LogCommand, LogBarrier, and LogConfiguration above protocol version 2), so the batch count is computed from observed log contents.
excluded: Multi-voter clusters, network faults and on-disk (bolt) log stores are excluded; the mechanism under test is in the startup replay path, not in replication.
The FSM's own semantics are excluded: MockFSM only records applied logs, and no FSM behavior is asserted.
No production code is modified and no full-package test suite is run; only the TestAssurance-prefixed test in this harness is selected.

parameters.predicted_boundary: ceil(fsm_bound_entries_in_window / max_append_entries) <= fsm_mutate_ch_capacity (128) returns; one batch more does not return

prefix.before: Each case builds one real single-voter cluster with opts{Peers:1, Bootstrap:true, CommitTrackingLogs:true} so the log store, stable store, snapshot store and FSM are produced by the target itself: the leader dispatches and commits the applied commands through the normal leaderLoop/dispatchLogs path, which stages the commit index via StageCommitIndex and stores the entries. Before shutdown the harness reads the store's persisted commit index, the last log index, cap(fsmMutateCh), the configured MaxAppendEntries, and censuses the entry types in the replay window with GetLog using the same rule as Raft.prepareLog. For the snapshot case it takes a user snapshot before shutdown and uses that snapshot's index as the restart's last-applied point. It then calls leader.Shutdown(), creates a fresh NewInmemTransport on the same address, and calls NewRaft over the unchanged logs/stable/snapshots instances as the target's own restart tests do, in a goroutine that reports completion through a channel; the harness waits up to 5s and, if nothing arrived, samples all goroutine stacks and keeps the one on the startup replay path. No production code is modified; the harness only reads state and drives the exported lifecycle.
prefix.after: Each case builds one real single-voter cluster with opts{Peers:1, Bootstrap:true, CommitTrackingLogs:true} so the log store, stable store, snapshot store and FSM are produced by the target itself: the leader dispatches and commits the applied commands through the normal leaderLoop/dispatchLogs path, which stages the commit index via StageCommitIndex and stores the entries. Before shutdown the harness reads the store's persisted commit index, the last log index, cap(fsmMutateCh), the configured MaxAppendEntries, and censuses the entry types in the replay window with GetLog using the same rule as Raft.prepareLog, then emits the startup_replay_prefix event. For the snapshot case it takes a user snapshot before shutdown and uses that snapshot's index as the restart's last-applied point. It then calls leader.Shutdown(), creates a fresh NewInmemTransport on the same address, and calls NewRaft over the unchanged logs/stable/snapshots instances as the target's own restart tests do, in a goroutine that reports completion through a channel; the harness waits up to 5s, and if nothing arrived it samples all goroutine stacks and keeps the one on the startup replay path. It then emits the startup_replay_restart event carrying the same operands plus replay_batches_within_capacity and the outcome. All events are printed as CA_EVENT JSON objects with an event name so they are extracted as observations rather than parse errors.

after.description: When the admitted startup replay window needs at most fsm_mutate_ch_capacity batches, the restart returns.
When the admitted startup replay window needs more than fsm_mutate_ch_capacity batches, NewRaft does not return within the bounded wait and a goroutine is left in the startup replay path.

experiments.revision_reason: The predecessor harness emitted CA_EVENT payloads without an event name, so the retained run was recorded entirely as invalid_observation (parse loss, indices 0-4) and no comparison could be evaluated. This revision names the events, splits them into a pre-restart admission event and a restart result event so the restart outcome is admitted by an independently observed prefix, declares the two comparisons the hypothesis predicts, and adds two boundary cases that straddle 128 batches with otherwise identical setup.

scope.description: Three restart-only cases over the real hashicorp/raft single-voter node with the captured snapshot settings left in place (in-memory transport, real commit-tracking log store): commit with the actual leader, optionally place the newest snapshot with a real user snapshot at a chosen index, commit more entries, stop the node, then call NewRaft again over the unchanged stores with a fresh transport on the same address and record whether it returns.
assumptions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the documented opt-in configuration for the feature under test.

SnapshotThreshold, SnapshotInterval and MaxAppendEntries are not modified by the harness; their configured values are reported in the admission event so the reader can check that the defaults were in force.

The test runs for seconds, well inside the configured 120s snapshot interval, so the periodic check does not fire during the case; that is the situation in which the window is whatever accumulated since the newest snapshot, and the case without a snapshot is the situation of a node before its first periodic check.

A returning restart is expected in the millisecond range; the 5s wait is a ceiling for recording non-return, and non-return cases additionally carry the stack of the goroutine left in the startup replay path.
Restarted instances use a null logger so no logging occurs after the test completes; logging is not part of the observed mechanism.
excluded: Real-time accumulation over a full 120s interval is not observed; the accumulation is produced deterministically by the target's own apply path instead, and the rate at which the same accumulation would occur in time is left as arithmetic on the configured interval.
Multi-voter clusters, network faults, on-disk log stores and FSM slowness are excluded.
No production code is modified and no full-package suite is run; only the TestAssurance-prefixed test in this harness is selected.

basis.prefix: Each case builds one real single-voter cluster with opts{Peers:1, Bootstrap:true, CommitTrackingLogs:true} and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, leaving SnapshotThreshold=8192, SnapshotInterval=120s and MaxAppendEntries=64 as configured. Commands are applied through the leader's normal path, with a real user snapshot (leader.Snapshot()) inserted after the chosen number of applies when a case asks for one, so the newest snapshot in the store and the entries above it are produced by the target itself. It finally emits the startup_replay_restart event carrying the same operands plus replay_batches_within_capacity and the outcome.

comparisons.description: With the configured snapshot settings in force, a restart whose committed-but-unapplied window needs at most fsm_mutate_ch_capacity batches returns.

experiments.revision_reason: Changed basis to address the recorded counterevidence: the predecessor disabled automatic snapshotting (SnapshotThreshold=MaxUint64, SnapshotInterval=1h) and varied MaxAppendEntries and applied counts; this revision leaves SnapshotThreshold, SnapshotInterval and MaxAppendEntries at their configured values, reports them as observed operands, places the newest snapshot with a real user snapshot at a chosen point, and includes a case with no snapshot at all. The comparisons are the same predicates over the same admission prefix shape, so the receipt answers whether the configured snapshot cadence keeps the window below the bound.

materials.text:
applyCh:               applyCh,
		fsm:                   fsm,
		fsmMutateCh:           make(chan interface{}, 128),
		fsmSnapshotCh:         make(chan *reqSnapshotFuture),
		leaderCh:              make(chan bool, 1),

func DefaultConfig() *Config {
	return &Config{
		ProtocolVersion:    ProtocolVersionMax,
		HeartbeatTimeout:   1000 * time.Millisecond,
		ElectionTimeout:    1000 * time.Millisecond,
		CommitTimeout:      50 * time.Millisecond,
		MaxAppendEntries:   64,
		ShutdownOnRemove:   true,
		TrailingLogs:       10240,
		SnapshotInterval:   120 * time.Second,
		SnapshotThreshold:  8192,
		LeaderLeaseTimeout: 500 * time.Millisecond,
		LogLevel:           "DEBUG",
	}
}
